items.area: crates/vilan-core/src/context.rs, crates/vilan-core/src/transformer.rs, the passes after threading (call-graph build, async inference, the const pass)
items.body: The context analysis itself moved by 3.6M instructions. The rest is downstream: the wraps and `None` arguments are new entities that threading, the call-graph build, async inference and the const pass each walk. Ideas, none tried: lower an absent context as a shared constant rather than a fresh `None` entity per site; wrap once per caller rather than per call; skip the later passes for the synthetic nodes. Keep every `b740_*` pin green and the corpus byte-identical. Retire the bump row if the cost goes.

items.title: False refusal: a trait default calling `self.note()` through `T: Note`, two levels deep, is refused although only covered code selects the strict impl
items.discussion: found by lane b740-58 (Order 58, 2026-11-12) beside B740; not caused by it; repro `scripts/integration/sweeps/order58/repros/b742-false-refusal.vl` with the checker's output beside it
items.body: B737 resolves a default's bound dispatch per call site, with a fallback to every candidate where the answer is not on record (a receiver-less `self.gap(..)` that may select an override). Two levels of such forwarding fall back although the instantiations on record say only covered code selects the strict candidate: only `announced(Deep {})` reaches `Deep::note`'s strict `depth.get()`, and that call sits under `depth.run(5, ..)`; the one call without the context, `announced(Plain {})`, selects `Plain::note`, which reads nothing; the refinement does not resolve the default's `self.note()` per entry when it is reached through the bounded `announced<T: Note>`, so it blames that call. Decide whether the refinement can carry the binding through the second level; pin the repro and the one-level form that already works.

items.title: `permutation_differential`'s corpus test runs 400 to 670 s on this box against a 900 s timeout, and timed out under load 32
items.discussion: integrator's full suite on next 12a04517 (2026-11-12) with four suites running at once: 11,627 of 11,628 passed, this one timed out at 900.13 s; alone it passed in 401 s; earlier runs the same day: 451 s, 610 s, 670 s
items.body: `the_corpus_as_modules_answers_the_same_under_every_permutation` is one test over the whole corpus. Options: split it by corpus program so nextest spreads it over cores and a slow machine fails one small case, not the whole; or raise its timeout override. Splitting is the better instrument (the suite's wall time is bounded by this one test today). Not a correctness problem.
